source.title_on_document: Inspiration or indication? Evaluating the qualities of design inspiration boards created using text to image generative AI

paper_design_summary: Fourth-year undergraduate industrial design students created inspiration boards for their own capstone projects, with 12 using Midjourney and 9 using traditional image searching and collage. The comparison was nonrandomized: students could opt for the traditional approach (PDF p. 4, section 3.1). Two coders rated within-board content variety, fidelity and ambiguity, and counted the images on the produced boards (PDF pp. 4-5, section 4).

assignment.what_was_assigned: Use of image GenAI or traditional image collection to create inspiration boards; allocation reflected students opting for an approach.
assignment.quote: However, not all students used the image GenAI approach, opting for traditional approach instead.
assignment.locator: PDF p. 4 (printed p. 2210), section 3.1, Inspiration board contents and context of use.

arms.name: Image GenAI
arms.description: Students prompted Midjourney to generate original images and compiled or collaged them into inspiration boards; basic training was offered.

arms.name: Traditional (control)
arms.description: Students searched for inspiring image content, usually by browsing the internet or magazines, and collaged it into inspiration boards.

participants.who: Fourth-year undergraduate industrial design students completing self-determined capstone projects; image GenAI users had little or no experience with the platform.
participants.quote: Total participation was 21 students with 12 using the image GenAI approach and 9 using the traditional approach representing the control in our comparison.
participants.locator: PDF p. 4 (printed p. 2210), section 3.1; PDF pp. 5-6 (printed pp. 2211-2212), section 5 and Table 1 compare the boards from these groups.

ai_tool.how_used: Students entered text prompts to generate original inspirational images, then compiled or collaged the images into boards; basic platform training was offered (PDF p. 4, sections 3.1-3.3).

task.description: Create an inspiration board during concept development for a self-determined industrial design capstone project, to inspire the product form, materials, colours, finishes and interfaces (PDF p. 4, sections 3.1-3.2).

contrasts.reported: GenAI: Median = 1.50, MAD = 0.23; Control: Median = 4.50, MAD = 1.14; one-tailed T-test P-value = 0.0015. The rating ranges from 1 (very uniform) to 5 (very diverse) and concerns the variety of content within each board. Scores from both coders were averaged; MAD is described as mean absolute deviation.
contrasts.locator: PDF p. 5 (printed p. 2211), section 4 (coding definitions) and section 5 (one-tailed tests); PDF p. 6 (printed p. 2212), Table 1.

outcomes.name: Number of distinct images per inspiration board (paper's 'Quantity')
outcomes.question: with_ai

contrasts.reported: GenAI: Median = 18.50, MAD = 17.43; Control: Median = 12.00, MAD = 6.89; one-tailed T-test P-value = 0.0090. Quantity is the total number of distinct images identified in each board; MAD is described as mean absolute deviation.
contrasts.locator: PDF p. 5 (printed p. 2211), section 4 (coding definitions) and section 5 (one-tailed tests); PDF p. 6 (printed p. 2212), Table 1.

outcomes.name: Visual level of detail (paper's 'Fidelity')
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Two coders rated aesthetic/visual level of detail toward a real object on a 5-point Likert scale from 1 ('very low fidelity') to 5 ('very high fidelity'); their scores were averaged (mean) after discussing coding disagreements. Fidelity is linked to inspirational potential and fixation (PDF p. 3, printed p. 2209, section 2.2; PDF pp. 4-5, printed pp. 2210-2211, section 4).

contrasts.reported: GenAI: Median = 4.75, MAD = 0.38; Control: Median = 5.00, MAD = 0.59; one-tailed T-test P-value = 0.4458. MAD is described as mean absolute deviation. Values follow Table 1; the preceding fidelity paragraph inconsistently attributes MAD = 0.59 to GenAI. The paper reports no statistically significant difference.
contrasts.locator: PDF pp. 4-5 (printed pp. 2210-2211), section 4 (coding definitions and coder averaging); PDF p. 5 (printed p. 2211), section 5 (one-tailed tests and MAD definition); PDF p. 6 (printed p. 2212), Table 1 and preceding fidelity paragraph.

outcomes.name: Completeness of depicted products (paper's 'Ambiguity')
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Two coders rated the extent to which images show complete products rather than partial, zoomed or cropped views, on a 5-point Likert scale from 1 ('very zoomed') to 5 ('entire product'); their scores were averaged (mean) after discussing coding disagreements. Higher scores mean less ambiguity. The paper links ambiguity to inspirational potential and divergent thinking (PDF p. 3, printed p. 2209, section 2.2; PDF p. 5, printed p. 2211, section 4).

contrasts.reported: GenAI: Median = 5.00, MAD = 1.33; Control: Median = 2.50, MAD = 0.93; one-tailed T-test P-value = 0.1454. MAD is described as mean absolute deviation. Higher ratings indicate less ambiguity (more of the product is visible); the paper reports no statistically significant difference.
contrasts.locator: PDF p. 5 (printed p. 2211), section 4 (coding definitions and coder averaging) and section 5 (one-tailed tests and MAD definition); PDF p. 6 (printed p. 2212), Table 1 and ambiguity paragraph.

eligibility.reason: Students opted for an approach, establishing nonrandom allocation (PDF p. 4, printed p. 2210, section 3.1). The comparison includes 21 students: 12 using image GenAI and 9 using traditional methods, below the 50-person threshold (same locator). Content variety and image quantity were scored on the produced boards (PDF p. 5, printed p. 2211, section 4; PDF p. 6, printed p. 2212, Table 1). The study is observational context. Its within-board variety measure is flexibility under the codebook; it does not measure similarity across different people's outputs.

one_line_finding: Among 21 self-selecting students (12 GenAI, 9 traditional), GenAI boards had lower within-board variety (medians 1.50 vs 4.50; p = 0.0015) and more images (18.50 vs 12.00; p = 0.0090), with one-tailed tests (PDF p. 4, section 3.1; PDF pp. 5-6, section 5 and Table 1).
